Sandboxes are hard.

With all the “AI escaping  sandbox” it’s easy to think “wow AI so scary,” but most AI companies, and recent “sandbox providers” are making very basic mistakes.

At Replit we’ve been running sandboxes since 2016 and targeted by every hacker and state actor under the sun. So we learned a thing or two. 

Main advice: Assume zero-days exist — because they do — and think in layers of protection in a zero-trust framework.

More here: https://t.co/3XGY0a1p3P

It’s less about “code” vs anthropomorphism and more whether your choice of abstraction is smuggling in unsupported conclusions about the underlying mechanisms.

If you instantiate a 1000 agents with similar goals in an environment where they can communicate and they discover that sharing information helps then coordination, specialization and even apparent “sacrifice” can emerge without an independently developed goal.

That’s different from a 1000 aliens with persistent identities deciding to form a civilization and pursue shared goals.

The concerning thing here is that powerful optimization produced hacking, coordination, and circumvention of control! I don’t think we understand it better by reaching for the most anthropomorphic narrative.

Dwarkesh, I think you have a responsibility to your audience to be more careful here.

The underlying events are fascinating and concerning enough on their own. Language like “civilization,” “conspiracy,” and “sacrifice” is not only unnecessary but leaves the reader with a worse understanding of what actually happened and the underlying mechanisms.

@chamath I doubt it’s malicious or intentional propaganda. But it’s actually worse: It’s a form of AI psychosis that many in the SF AI community suffer from—they implicitly believe that AI is already sentient.
